questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I chose to go to Unimelb due to the fact, that they had some excellent courses within the areas I find Interesting. Furthermore, the university is highly respected world wide.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I absolutely loved my exchange semester. Cannot recommend it enough.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was quite easy. Unimelb has an excellent website, and you can find answers to most questions just by searching "question bla bla" unimelb. The universities (ucph and unimelb) both help you alot with relevant information.

questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I am fully aware that prior exchange students has written that it was okay to found housing when arriving in Melbourne. Nevertheless, I would not say that this is the case anymore (maybe due to covid or some other factors.). The housing market in Melbourne is incredibly expensive, and for student who will only be here for < 6 months finding housing through flatmates, fairy floss etc. is extremely difficult and competitive. This implies that many end up living in places like Unilodge, Yugo or Scape, which is great but expensive. The housing provided by uni is as expensive as the three aforementioned "companies".

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Very easy.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: There is a time period in which the univeristiy allows you to change courses (2 weeks ish). This is great, as you get to see the professors, and experience lectures in order to get an idea whether the course is something for you.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Stop1 was good assistance.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got the ones I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Relax, and go to different courses the first week to see what they have to offer.

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Macroeconometrics (ECOM90007)
Derivative Securities (FNCE90011)
Investment Management (FNCE90056)
Applied Risk Management (FNCE90082)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Macroeconometrics was a roller coaster. I loved the course and the professor is absoltely fantastic, however, it is extremely time consuming as well as complex, and one should really keep this in mind before taking it. However, I learned a lot and have no regrets, although you might be more stressed then your fellow exchange students. Derivatives was very intuition based compared to UCPH, which was fun to experience. The professor was great. The last two courses I did not like to much, but I learned alot about various financial products which I would not have been able to in Cph.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Do it, you will love it. Connect with the remaining danes before heading to melb, we had a great group of people. Travel whenever you have the option to do so, even though you did not emagining going there prior to departure. I did not think I would go to Tassy, but it was stunning.
